column1: Georeference: First Ypres, the sketch maps of the British official history
How the Ypres sketch maps of the British official history were tied to the current map

Sketch A (the Ypres area) is bound across two pages; about a kilometre of ground is lost in the binding between them, so each page was fitted on its own: a shift, a turn and one scale, from villages that are both on the sketch and in OpenStreetMap (S39). The dated sketches were fitted the same way, each on its own, allowing a slightly different scale across and down the page.

The misfit is the typical distance between where the fit puts a village and where OpenStreetMap has it. It mixes three things: the sketch is generalised, my reading of each village symbol is good to about 50 m, and a village is not a point.
